# Statement of Reproducibility {#sec-reproducibility}

This thesis follows the FAIR principles for data and code management specified in the ZHAW Statement of Reproducibility.

## Code and Workflow

The analytical workflow is split across two components. The resistance surface pipeline, from raw telemetry to the final 25-metre resistance raster, is contained in the single Jupyter notebook `scripts/01_create_resistance_surface.ipynb`. Given the same input data and software environment, this notebook produces identical outputs deterministically. All connectivity analyses, including the infection-risk kernel, the biased correlated random walk, and the iSSF-based individual movement model, are implemented directly in the QGIS plugin *Wildboar Connectivity (ASF)*. The plugin is distributed as a standard QGIS Python package with a `metadata.txt` manifest and can be installed through the QGIS plugin manager.

## Software Environment

The ecological algorithm was developed in R 4.5.1 using `terra` 1.9.11, `sf` 1.1.0,
`amt` 0.3.1.0, `survival` 3.8.3, `broom` 1.0.10, `car`, and the tidyverse packages
`dplyr`, `tidyr`, `purrr`, and `lubridate`. The plugin was implemented for QGIS 3.40.13
in Python. Core spatial operations relied on `rasterio` 1.4.3 (raster I/O and
rasterization), `numpy` 1.26.2 (array manipulation and resistance editing), `scipy`
1.12.0 (connected-component labeling via `scipy.ndimage` and the sparse Laplacian
fallback solver via `scipy.sparse`), and `scikit-image` 0.25.1 (least-cost path
tracing via `skimage.graph.MCP_Geometric`). The QGIS framework itself (PyQGIS, PyQt5)
is bundled with QGIS 3.40.13 and is not a pip-installed dependency. Circuit-theory
analysis was performed by Circuitscape.jl invoked through a Julia subprocess, with
the scipy sparse solver as a pure-Python fallback.

## Directory Structure

The project follows a standard structure with separate directories for raw, temporary, and processed data (`data/raw`, `data/temp`, `data/processed`). Each transformation step is documented in the commented notebooks above.

## Data Availability

All base geodata are drawn from publicly accessible Swiss federal services. The GPS telemetry and the permanent ASP fence shapefile were provided by the project partners and are not publicly redistributable. See @tbl-datasets in the data sources appendix for the full list of inputs and providers.
